title: When the Scholarship Breaks
premise: Felix Eriksen, the invisible statistician of Ashgrove High's legendary hockey program, notices that a group chat called 'The Roster' is posting predictions of games, accidents, and auditions before they happen—and every prediction comes true. The chat traces back to the Founders' Scholarship, a town tradition that secretly selects one student each year to carry forward the founders' legacy, and it wants Felix to play its game: feed it data, and it will guarantee his escape from Ashgrove. As classmates who refuse to participate begin losing memories of the tradition itself—then of each other—Felix realizes the scholarship survives by consuming the futures of the students it 'saves.' In the final audition, Felix must choose between a guaranteed exit and destroying the tradition, and he chooses destruction, burning the selection ledger so the town must remember its own history instead of outsourcing it.
about_author: Sable Kavanagh grew up in a mill town where high school sports were the only industry that never closed, and she has been auditing small-town mythologies ever since. She writes young adult fiction about kids who do the math nobody else will.

chapters.title: Margin of Error
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Establishes Felix as the team's uncredited statistician who has found impossible patterns in game outcomes—injuries scheduled like appointments. He counts down 94 days to graduation, invisible by design. Emotional beat: weary resignation sharpening into suspicion when a stat he never shared appears in an unknown group chat, posted before the game it describes.

chapters.title: The Roster
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The group chat adds him without invitation; members are all scholarship-adjacent students, including Priya Nair, the editor who remembers things no one else does. The chat predicts a locker-room fire drill two hours early. Emotional beat: uncanny dread mixed with the intoxicating first taste of being chosen rather than overlooked.

chapters.title: Ninety-Four Days
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Priya shows Felix the Founders' Scholarship archive: every 'recipient' left town rich and free, and every one is missing from alumni memories except hers. She's kept a private ledger for years. Emotional beat: conspiratorial intimacy—the relief of finally being believed, shadowed by fear of what remembering costs her.

chapters.title: Home Ice
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The chat offers Felix a deal: keep feeding it data and it guarantees his out-of-state tuition, his escape. His mother's overtime shifts make the offer ache. Meanwhile teammate Denny, who mocked the chat, forgets his own birthday mid-practice. Emotional beat: temptation versus loyalty; Felix accepts provisionally, telling himself he's playing double agent.

chapters.title: What Denny Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Priya. The memory losses accelerate and spread—Denny now can't recall why he loved hockey at all. Priya discovers the ledger lists names under two columns: Saved and Spent. Spent names are erased from the town's collective memory to fuel the predictions. Emotional beat: grief and fury; the stakes shift from personal survival to protecting everyone.

chapters.title: Audition Season
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The chat announces this year's final audition—a public ceremony during the championship game where the new recipient will be named. It pressures Felix to nominate someone else, dangling his mother's debts. He feeds it false data as sabotage, but the chat corrects itself instantly, showing it already knows everything he knows. Emotional beat: the trap closing; powerlessness inside apparent privilege.

chapters.title: Spent
chapters.summary: POV Priya. A name in the Spent column becomes real: Marcus, last year's runner-up, is gone—no photos, no records, his family vaguely grieving something they can't name. Only Priya's ledger proves he existed. The chat warns her that archivists are always spent eventually. Emotional beat: terror crystallizing into resolve; she copies the ledger and hides it with Felix.

chapters.title: The Long Change
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix recruits Denny—restored slightly by distance from the rink—to rig the championship scoreboard and sound system so the audition can't run cleanly. The chat retaliates by erasing Felix's own statistics career, retroactively making him 'never on the roster.' Emotional beat: sacrifice; Felix loses his carefully built invisibility's only compensation and finds he doesn't miss it.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: POV Felix and Priya alternating. At the championship ceremony, the chat offers Felix the recipient's chair one last time: leave tonight, debt-free, memory intact. He walks to the podium, reads the Spent column aloud—including Marcus—and Priya broadcasts the ledger over the arena speakers while Denny kills the lights. The tradition requires belief to function; the town, hearing itself, refuses. Emotional beat: climax—public truth-telling as the only weapon the powerless have.

chapters.title: Overtime
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Weeks later: memories return in fragments, Marcus's family gets their son back into their grief, and the scholarship fund is dissolved into need-based aid. The chat goes silent, though one final message reads simply 'noted.' Felix graduates on ordinary merit, unremarkable and present. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—the price was paid, the future is unwritten, and being visible turns out to be survivable.
